questions.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}2xy \\ {e}^{xy}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy)=2y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy)=2x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xy})=y{e}^{xy},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xy})=x{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2y & 2x \\ y{e}^{xy} & x{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+1},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+1})=-\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+1)^{2}},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+1})=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+1)^{2}} & \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=0,\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-0=[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
0+0+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=y\operatorname{tan}⁡x,\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{4} \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{4} \\ 2\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{tan}⁡x)=\frac{y}{{cos}^{2}⁡x},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{tan}⁡x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{{cos}^{2}⁡x} & \operatorname{tan}⁡x\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{4} \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=2,\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-2=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{4} \\ 2\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
2+4+1=7.
$$

questions.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}xy \\ {x}^{2}-y \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y & \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} \\ \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} & -1 \\ \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} & x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}].
$$

From top to bottom, what are the missing entries?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)=y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)=x, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-y)=2x,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-y)=-1, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))=y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy),\, & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))=x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y & x \\ 2x & -1 \\ y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy) & x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}].
$$

Thus, the missing entries are $x,\,$ $2x,\,$ and $y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy).$

questions.problem:
Consider the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}} \\ {e}^{{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}^{2}}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

If the linear approximation of $f$ at  $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}1 \\ ∗\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}∗ & 1 \\ 1 & ∗\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]),
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({e}^{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}})=2{x}_{1}{e}^{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({e}^{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}})={e}^{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({e}^{{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}^{2}})={e}^{{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}^{2}},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({e}^{{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}^{2}})=-2{x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}{e}^{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}} & {e}^{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}} \\ {e}^{{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}^{2}} & -2{x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
1+2+2=5.
$$
